findings.title: Apply the owner-directory check before refusing quarantine
findings.reason: Fixed in `65f77f2`. Confirmed: a record whose metadata is internally valid but whose persisted owner ID does not bind to its directory key was rejected by enumeration and accepted as readable here, so the doctor routed the operator to a remedy that refused it.

findings.title: Quarantine invalid recovery journals without promoting them
findings.reason: Fixed in `65f77f2`. Confirmed: with no active directory and an invalid `.old` journal, `recoverSwap` fails, which blocked enumeration and made `QuarantineApp` exit before collecting the journal — the record was unreachable by the only remedy for it.

findings.title: Sync the quarantine destination before the source
findings.reason: Fixed in `f5d9b22`. Confirmed and accepted: a cross-directory rename whose source removal is persisted before the destination entry turns a crash between the two syncs into credential loss, which contradicts the whole point of preserving rather than deleting the record.

findings.title: Apply the complete enumeration gate before refusing quarantine
findings.reason: Fixed in `f5d9b22`, taking the second of the two options you offered — stop routing those failures to the quarantine remedy — rather than widening the shared gate. The disagreement you found is real, and it was mine: the round-1 sweep over-applied "attribute every per-record failure" to `clearSwapLeftovers`, which is not a readability failure.

findings.title: Preserve the unreadable record owner for missing keys
findings.reason: Fixed in `e7512ff`. Confirmed: a record present but missing `app.pem` wraps `ErrNoAppCredentials`, which the switch matched before the sentinel, so the finding came back as `missing_machine_key` with owner zero — precisely the "which record is blocking everything?" question this PR exists to answer.

findings.title: Reject keystore-wide failures before quarantining an owner
findings.reason: Fixed in `6d0f41f`. Confirmed: `assertPermissionsAt` asserts `k.root` and `k.dir` alongside the record's own directory, so a widened mode on either fails the load gate for every registration alike — and withdrawal then read that as "this record is unreadable" and moved a perfectly good registration out of janitor coverage over a directory mode, while leaving enumeration just as blocked.

findings.title: Make multi-source quarantine failure atomic
findings.reason: Fixed in `d250168`. Confirmed, though the wedge arrives by a slightly different route than described, and the route matters for the fix.

findings.title: Avoid routing post-promotion cleanup failures to quarantine
findings.reason: Fixed in `34adc76`. Confirmed, and this is the round-2 cleanup class recurring through a second call site — recovery clears the journals itself after promoting a record, and my earlier sweep narrowed only the outer call site.

findings.title: Make quarantine resumable after directory-sync failures
findings.reason: Fixed in `facdd96`, with one part of the suggestion declined on merits. Confirmed: with every rename landed and a directory sync failing, nothing remained to move, so the retry took the `len(sources) == 0` path and reported a missing record instead of finishing the sequence.

findings.title: Retry the source sync after discarding an invalid stage
findings.reason: Declining this one, with a reason rather than a fix. The trace is accurate: an invalid `.staging` discarded by `recoverSwap` whose `syncDir(k.dir)` then fails leaves no source and no quarantine record, so a retry returns `ErrNoAppRegistration` without re-issuing that sync.

findings.title: Persist journal renames before moving the active record
findings.reason: Fixed in `6823ccd`. Confirmed, and it is a gap in my own round-5 reasoning rather than a new surface.

findings.title: Refuse quarantine when any owner suffix already exists
findings.reason: Real, and filed as #280 rather than fixed here. The suggested narrow remedy cannot be taken on its own, which is the reason.

findings.title: Keep recovery permission failures out of record quarantine
findings.reason: Fixed in `7e667a9`. Confirmed, and it is the round-4 class recurring from the opposite direction — my sweep there was one-directional, which is a miss rather than convergence.

findings.title: Require search permission before advertising quarantine
findings.reason: Fixed in `3e9de30`. Confirmed, and this is the third member of one class, so I stopped fixing members and stated the invariant.

findings.title: Check withdrawal roots before attributing load failures
findings.reason: Fixed in `bda8d2f`. Confirmed, and the predicate was right while its placement was the miss: round 12 put the keystore-wide gate on the recovery-failure attribution and not on the ordinary load-failure attribution, so a damaged active record under an unwritable root was still attributed and still routed to a remedy that refuses.

findings.title: Sync each journal withdrawal before moving the next
findings.reason: Fixed in `315cc86`. Confirmed, and the round-9 barrier was conditioned on the wrong thing: it persisted the journal moves only when an active record was also moving, so a state with no active directory — invalid `.old` blocking recovery, valid `.staging` alongside — skipped it entirely and could resurrect exactly what the operator withdrew.

findings.title: Gate attribution on the quarantine destination
findings.reason: Fixed in `c184094`. Confirmed: an existing quarantine directory the owner cannot write into fails every rename exactly as a deficient source root does, and the gate listed only the two roots, so the record was attributed and the remedy refused.

findings.title: Reject over-wide quarantine roots before owner attribution
findings.reason: Fixed in `cea7961`. Confirmed, and it is an asymmetry I introduced myself: splitting the check into one helper for attribution and one for the withdrawal left attribution testing only owner access, so a too-permissive destination was accepted there and rejected by the withdrawal.

findings.title: Reject malformed quarantine targets before attributing owners
findings.reason: Fixed in `57019c5`, and I stopped fixing members of this class and closed it structurally instead. Confirmed: a file or symlink where the owner's target directory belongs passes every directory-mode check and still makes the rename impossible, so the record was attributed and the remedy refused.
